clinicalPearls: A mutilating palmoplantar keratoderma characterised by a distinctive honeycomb (honeycomb-patterned) hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
Starfish-shaped (stellate) keratoses over the knuckles and dorsa of the digits are a highly suggestive sign
Constricting fibrous bands (pseudo-ainhum) form around digits and can progress to autoamputation
The classic form is associated with sensorineural deafness and results from dominant GJB2 (connexin 26) mutations
A variant form (Camisa) has associated ichthyosis and is caused by loronin mutations in the LOR gene
Onset is usually in infancy or early childhood with progression of the keratoderma over time
Management is supportive with emollients/keratolytics and oral retinoids, with surgical release of constricting bands to prevent digital loss
reference.pathophysiology: Vohwinkel syndrome exists in two genetically distinct forms. The classic form with deafness is caused by dominant mutations in GJB2 encoding connexin 26, a gap-junction protein; abnormal gap-junction channels disturb epidermal cell-to-cell communication and cochlear function. The variant form associated with ichthyosis arises from mutations in LOR encoding loricrin, a major component of the cornified cell envelope, leading to defective envelope assembly and abnormal terminal differentiation of keratinocytes. In both, disordered keratinisation produces the honeycomb keratoderma and stellate keratoses, and progressive fibrous constriction (pseudo-ainhum) around digits can strangulate them, causing autoamputation.
additionalInvestigations: Skin biopsy showing orthohyperkeratosis and, in the loricrin variant, retained nuclei within the stratum corneum
Molecular genetic testing of GJB2 and LOR
Audiological assessment for sensorineural hearing loss (classic form)
Clinical and photographic monitoring of digital constriction bands
Radiographs of digits where bony involvement or impending autoamputation is suspected
Assessment for associated ichthyosis in the variant form
redFlags: Progressive pseudo-ainhum threatening digital viability or autoamputation
Secondary infection or ulceration of fissured keratotic skin
New or worsening hearing loss requiring audiological input
Functional impairment of the hands limiting activity
reference.prognosis: The keratoderma is chronic and progressive, and the principal threat is loss of digits from constricting bands. With emollient/keratolytic care, oral retinoids and timely surgical band release, digital function can often be preserved, though the condition is not curable.
pitfalls: Failing to recognise and release pseudo-ainhum bands early, allowing digital autoamputation
Not distinguishing the deafness-associated (GJB2) form from the ichthyosis (loricrin) variant, which affects counselling
Overlooking the honeycomb pattern and stellate knuckle keratoses that distinguish it from other keratodermas
Reliance on keratolytics alone when retinoids and surgery may be needed
